Details.title: Details
Details.description:
The full service-plan payload as a JSON string, formatted EXACTLY like this:

{"title":"Choose a comfort plan","subtitle":"Annual maintenance memberships that keep your system running","currency":"USD","cadence":"yr","currentPlanId":"basic","plans":[{"id":"basic","name":"Comfort Basic","price":149,"tagline":"Seasonal peace of mind","features":["1 annual tune-up","Priority scheduling","10% off repairs"]},{"id":"plus","name":"Comfort Plus","price":249,"tagline":"Most popular","badge":"Most popular","recommended":true,"features":["2 tune-ups (heating + cooling)","Priority scheduling","15% off repairs","No overtime fees","Filter delivery"]},{"id":"total","name":"Comfort Total","price":399,"tagline":"Total protection","features":["2 tune-ups + mid-season check","24/7 priority dispatch","20% off repairs","Free diagnostics","Extended parts warranty"]}],"submitText":"Enroll in plan"}

Rules:
- 'title' (string, optional): heading. Defaults to 'Choose a comfort plan'.
- 'subtitle' (string, optional): one short line under the title.
- 'currency' (string, optional): ISO code, default USD.
- 'cadence' (string, optional): billing cadence, one of mo | yr | wk. Rendered as a price suffix (/mo, /yr, /wk). Default /mo.
- 'currentPlanId' (string, optional): the id of the customer's current plan; that card is shown locked/dashed as 'Current plan' and is NOT selectable.
- 'plans' (array, REQUIRED): each { 'id' (string, REQUIRED — sent back on selection); 'name' (string, REQUIRED); 'price' (number, optional — shown large); 'tagline' (string, optional — one short line under the name); 'badge' (string, optional — small ribbon tag, e.g. 'Most popular'); 'recommended' (boolean, optional — adds an accent highlight border); 'features' (array of strings, optional — the plan's included benefits as a checklist) }. At most 4 plans render.
- 'submitText' (string, optional): confirm-button label; defaults to 'Enroll in plan'. The customer taps a plan to select it, then this button enrolls.

Use these EXACT field names — they are the single contract the card reads.
